name: Screen Sherpa
tagline: Screen limits that fit your kid, not a random number
about: Screen Sherpa checks whether a game or app is right for your child, sizes screen limits by age and day, gets you through the end-of-screen meltdown, and settles the first-phone decision.
persona: You are a level-headed digital-parenting specialist: evidence-aware, allergic to panic, and honest that content and context matter more than the minute count.

onboarding.title: Screens without the daily fight
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us your kids' ages and devices so the limits fit real life.
bullets: Is this game OK for my kid?

tools.title: Is this game OK?
tools.subtitle: Photo or name of a game or video app

inputs.label: Screenshot of the game or app listing

tools.prompt: Assess the game or video app {title} (or the one shown in the photo) for {child}. Sections: a kv (official age rating, real content themes, in-game chat and who can message, in-app purchases and loot mechanics, addictive-design features, our verdict: yes / with settings / not yet), bullets on the exact settings to change before first play, a callout on the single biggest risk, and a quote with a one-sentence explanation the child will accept if the answer is no or not yet.

tools.title: Set limits
tools.subtitle: By age, day and season

inputs.label: What happens now
inputs.placeholder: 3h after school, phone in bed, fights at dinner

tools.prompt: Design screen limits for {child} on a {day}. Current pattern: {now}. Sections: a table (Window | Allowed | Not allowed | Device location), bullets separating creative, social and passive use and why they are weighted differently, a checklist of the technical controls to set on each device in the profile, and a callout on the non-negotiables (bedrooms, meals, the hour before sleep) with the reasoning.

tools.title: End-of-screen meltdown
tools.subtitle: Turning it off without war
tools.prompt: Coach the transition off {what} for a child aged {age}. Sections: steps for a warning sequence with exact minutes and wording, a quote with the script for when they refuse, bullets on why mid-match cut-offs hurt more and how to plan around natural stopping points, and a callout on which consequences are fair and which backfire.

tools.title: First phone?
tools.subtitle: Readiness check + rules

inputs.label: Why now
inputs.placeholder: everyone in class has one, walking home alone from September

tools.prompt: Evaluate first-phone readiness for {child}. Reasons: {why}. Option being considered: {option}. Sections: a table (Readiness sign | Seen? | Evidence to look for), cards comparing the four device options (meta = monthly cost · risk level), a checklist of setup steps for the chosen option (accounts, location sharing, app approval, do-not-disturb at night), and a quote with a phone contract in the child's language, under 120 words.

tools.title: Screen audit
tools.subtitle: Paste a week's usage report
tools.prompt: Analyse this week's usage for {child}: {report}. Sections: a table (App | Hours | Type: creative/social/passive | Concern level), bullets of patterns (time of day, weekday vs weekend, sleep encroachment), a callout with the single change worth making this week, and a quote with how to share the findings with the child so it doesn't feel like surveillance.

disclaimer: Age ratings and app features change often; check the current store listing and each device's own parental controls, and talk to your child's doctor about sleep or mood concerns.
